factual_and_methodological.summary: Core chronology, fiscal correction, hyperinflation mechanism and post-stabilization interpretation were checked against NBER/IMF/World Bank evidence. The IMF record corroborates the August 29, 1985 New Economic Policy and the central-administration cash-deficit reduction from above 20% to about 6.5% of GDP. The text distinguishes annual-average inflation from post-program high-frequency rates and avoids attributing employment/distribution outcomes solely to stabilization.

editorial_publication_readiness.opening: Direct thesis-led opening states the mechanism and transfer limit without generic summary scaffolding.
editorial_publication_readiness.headings: Headings identify causal mechanisms, observed outcomes, political economy, durability and transfer limits.
editorial_publication_readiness.language_localization: EN and PT-BR read natively and preserve technical meaning without internal labels or template language.
editorial_publication_readiness.repetition: No blocking repetition; caveats recur only where they perform distinct attribution or transfer-limit functions.
editorial_publication_readiness.cohesion: Progression runs from initial condition through institutional design, transmission, outcomes, distribution, implementation, durability and transfer limits.
editorial_publication_readiness.template_meta_qa: No prompt, QA-process or agent/template leakage detected.

contextual_depth.summary: Fiscal institutions, monetary financing, exchange-rate dynamics, labor conflict, mining restructuring and the tin-price shock are connected to the stabilization mechanism rather than presented ornamentally.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: Three analytical tables, one CPI bar chart and one causal flow; EN/PT-BR are semantically parallel.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: The annual CPI chart uses annual-average observations and is explicitly distinguished from the post-program inflation rate; attribution across simultaneous reforms remains limited.

contrary_evidence: The rapid disinflation does not isolate the independent effect of fiscal correction because exchange-rate, price, financial and public-sector reforms were implemented together.
Employment and regional-income losses cannot be attributed solely to anti-inflation policy because mining restructuring, pre-existing recession and the world tin-price collapse also mattered.
The case does not support generalizing abrupt fiscal contraction to lower-inflation economies with functioning debt markets and different monetary institutions.
limitations: Historical aggregates vary with institutional definition; the report appropriately qualifies the central-administration cash-deficit measure.
Annual CPI observations obscure within-year turning points during hyperinflation and are therefore complemented by higher-frequency historical evidence.
The package was implemented under an extreme fiscal-monetary regime, limiting external validity for ordinary inflation episodes.
notes: New policy-case publication candidate. Primary-source and high-quality historical evidence support the central claims; no public bundle for this ID was present at the reviewed HEAD.

en.title: Bolivia's 1985 stabilization: ending hyperinflation by breaking the fiscal-monetary loop
en.deck: The August 1985 program sharply reduced fiscal financing pressure while changing the exchange-rate, price and public-sector regime; hyperinflation ended quickly, but the wider restructuring carried distinct employment and distributional costs.
en.regime: Emergency stabilization of a fiscal-monetary hyperinflation through deficit correction, exchange-rate unification, monetary restraint and broader market reforms
en.key_risk: Treating the episode as a universal argument for abrupt fiscal contraction ignores the extreme monetary-financing regime and the social costs of the broader reform package.

pt-BR.title: A estabilização boliviana de 1985: encerrando a hiperinflação ao romper o circuito fiscal-monetário
pt-BR.deck: O programa de agosto de 1985 reduziu fortemente a pressão do financiamento fiscal e alterou o regime cambial, de preços e do setor público; a hiperinflação terminou rapidamente, mas a reestruturação mais ampla teve custos próprios sobre emprego e distribuição.
pt-BR.regime: Estabilização emergencial de hiperinflação fiscal-monetária por correção do déficit, unificação cambial, restrição monetária e reformas de mercado mais amplas
pt-BR.key_risk: Tratar o episódio como argumento universal por contração fiscal abrupta ignora o regime extremo de financiamento monetário e os custos sociais do pacote mais amplo.
